    [ search index=aap sourcetype=aap:api_access status=401 path="/api/*/login*"
      | bin _time span=15m
      | stats count as prior_failures by _time, user, src_ip
      | where prior_failures >= 5 ]
| table success_time, user, src_ip, prior_failures
tuning_guidance: Rare for humans; tune the failure threshold to your typical mistyped-password rate.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the account owner whether the login was expected.
Immediately review what job templates/credentials the account can access.
Check the account's activity stream for actions taken since the login.
response_guidance: Treat as a likely-compromised account: disable it, revoke its API tokens, and audit every job it could have launched.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New or Unexpected API Token Created
description: Detects creation of a new personal access token (PAT) for a Controller user. Tokens bypass interactive login (including any SSO/MFA enforced at the login page) and provide durable API access; an attacker with a foothold on an admin's authenticated session can create a token for themselves as a persistence mechanism that survives a subsequent password reset.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Token creation is logged as an activity-stream event tied to the acting and owning user.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream events for oauth2accesstoken creation.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream operation="create" object1="o_auth2_access_token"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "user=(?<token_owner>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, token_owner
tuning_guidance: Legitimate CI/CD pipeline setup creates tokens as a normal onboarding step; correlate with a documented integration change and expect the owner and actor to match for self-service token creation.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and token_owner - do they match, or did one user create a token for another (higher suspicion)?
Review the token's scope and expiration.
Check for API calls made using the new token immediately after creation.
response_guidance: Revoke unauthorized tokens immediately and investigate the actor account.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SSO/Authentication Backend Configuration Changed
description: Detects a change to Controller's SSO/authentication backend settings (SAML/OIDC/LDAP configuration), which controls how every user authenticates. A weakened or redirected configuration can enable an attacker to bypass the organization's normal identity controls (including MFA enforced upstream) entirely.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Setting-change events for authentication-related configuration categories.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream setting-update events scoped to SAML/OIDC/LDAP/authentication categories.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream operation="update" category="authentication"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "setting=(?<setting_name>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, setting_name
tuning_guidance: Planned IdP migrations or certificate renewals are the only expected source and should be tied to a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Diff the configuration for the exact change.
Identify the actor and confirm authorization.
Check for new logins immediately following the change, especially via a newly-added/modified identity provider.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately and force re-authentication for all users.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1556: Modify Authentication Process

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Machine Credential Created or Modified
description: Detects creation or modification of a machine (SSH) credential object. Machine credentials are what let AAP authenticate to managed RHEL hosts, often as root or a highly-privileged automation user; a new or altered credential is a direct path to fleet-wide access if attached to a job template. Secret material itself is never logged or exposed by this detection.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Credential create/update events, metadata only - never the secret value.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream events for credential object creation/modification.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="credential" (operation="create" OR operation="update")
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "credential_name=\"(?<credential_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, credential_name
tuning_guidance: Legitimate credential rotation and new-integration onboarding are expected sources; correlate with a documented rotation schedule or change ticket.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and the credential's type/scope.
Check which job templates/inventories the credential is (or becomes) associated with (AAP-008).
Confirm rotation was intentional if this is an update to an existing credential.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, delete/rotate the credential immediately and audit any job that used it.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Vault Credential Modified
description: Detects a change to an Ansible Vault password credential, which controls decryption of any vault-encrypted variables/files referenced by managed playbooks. Compromise here can expose every secret encrypted with that vault ID across every project using it.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Credential update events where credential_type=Vault.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream credential-update events scoped to Vault-type credentials.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="credential" operation="update" credential_type="Vault"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "credential_name=\"(?<credential_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, credential_name
tuning_guidance: Scheduled vault-password rotation is the expected legitimate source.
investigation_steps: Identify actor.
Confirm the change matches a documented rotation.
Check for subsequent job runs referencing vault-encrypted content.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, re-rotate the vault password and re-encrypt affected content, then investigate the actor.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Cloud Credential Created or Modified
description: Detects creation or modification of a cloud-provider credential (AWS/Azure/GCP/VMware). Compromise extends the blast radius beyond the RHEL fleet into whatever cloud infrastructure the credential can control - often with far greater destructive/financial potential than an on-prem SSH credential.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Credential create/update events for cloud credential types.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream credential events for cloud-provider credential types.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="credential" (operation="create" OR operation="update") (credential_type="Amazon Web Services" OR credential_type="Microsoft Azure Resource Manager" OR credential_type="Google Compute Engine" OR credential_type="VMware vCenter")
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, credential_type
tuning_guidance: Legitimate cloud-integration onboarding and scheduled key rotation are expected sources; correlate with cloud-provider-side key rotation records where available.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and credential scope.
Cross-reference with the cloud provider's own IAM audit trail for the corresponding key.
Check what inventories/job templates use the credential.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, revoke the cloud credential at the provider level immediately, not just within AAP.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1098.001: Additional Cloud Credentials

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Privileged Credential Newly Associated With a Job Template
description: Detects a credential being attached to a job template it was not previously associated with, especially a privileged machine credential added to a template with a broad inventory scope. This is the step that converts a stolen/weak credential from 'exists' to 'weaponizable' - anyone who can launch the template can now use the credential's access.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Job template association-change events.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream events for job-template credential association changes.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="job_template" operation="associate" object2="credential"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "template_name=\"(?<template_name>[^\"]+)\""
| rex field=_raw "credential_name=\"(?<credential_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, template_name, credential_name
tuning_guidance: Legitimate template configuration during onboarding is expected; escalate specifically when the resulting template's inventory scope is broad (many/all hosts) or when the actor is not the template's normal owner/maintainer.
investigation_steps: Identify the template's inventory scope and who can launch it.
Identify actor.
Check for a job launch immediately following the association.
response_guidance: Remove the association if unauthorized and audit any jobs already launched under the new configuration.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Job Template Modified to Enable Privilege Escalation
description: Detects a job template being modified to enable 'become' (Ansible's privilege-escalation mechanism, typically sudo to root) where it was previously disabled, or to change its become method/user to something more privileged. Converts a template that ran as an unprivileged user into one capable of full root-level changes on every targeted host.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Job template update events with the become_enabled field.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream job-template update events where become_enabled transitions from false to true.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="job_template" operation="update" "become_enabled"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "template_name=\"(?<template_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, template_name, _raw
tuning_guidance: Legitimate expansion of a template's operational scope (it now needs to manage a privileged resource) is the expected source; require change-ticket correlation for templates targeting production/broad inventories.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and the template's inventory scope.
Check whether the template's playbook source (project) was also recently changed (RH-X-004 supply-chain pattern).
Check for a job launch immediately after.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and review any jobs run with escalated privilege since the change.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1548: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Job Template Limit Widened to Broader Host Scope
description: Detects a job template's `limit` field (which restricts execution to a subset of its inventory) being removed or widened, expanding a previously narrowly-scoped template into one that can act against many more hosts than originally intended.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Job template update events with a changed limit field.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream job-template update events where the limit field changed to a broader (or empty/all) value.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="job_template" operation="update" "limit"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "template_name=\"(?<template_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, template_name, _raw
tuning_guidance: Operational needs legitimately change scope over time; escalate specifically when the new scope is empty (meaning the full inventory, potentially hundreds/thousands of hosts) versus a modestly wider host list.
investigation_steps: Identify the old and new scope.
Identify actor.
Check for a job launch immediately after the widening.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized before the next scheduled/triggered run.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Job Launched Using the shell or command Module
description: Detects a job run whose playbook invokes the `shell` or `command` module rather than an idempotent, purpose-built Ansible module. While a completely normal part of many legitimate playbooks, shell/command tasks are also how an attacker who has modified a project's playbook (RH-X-004) would most straightforwardly run arbitrary commands, so this is a valuable building-block signal for correlation rather than a standalone high-confidence alert.

data_sources.name: AAP job events
data_sources.description: Per-task job event records include the Ansible module used for each play task.

detection_logic: Filters job-event records for task_action=shell or task_action=command.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events (task_action="shell" OR task_action="command")
| table _time, job_id, template_name, task_name, task_action
tuning_guidance: Very common in legitimate playbooks; use as a correlation building block (feed into RH-X-003/RH-X-004) rather than a standalone alert, and reserve standalone alerting for shell/command tasks appearing in a template that was not expected to contain them (a sudden new task in a previously-reviewed playbook).
investigation_steps: Review the exact command executed.
Identify the template and who launched the job.
Check whether this task existed in the project's prior playbook revision or is newly introduced.
response_guidance: No standalone response for expected use; escalate per correlated detections if the command is destructive or unexpected.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Job Targeting All Hosts in Inventory
description: Detects a job launch with no host limit applied, meaning it targets every host in its inventory - potentially hundreds or thousands of RHEL systems in a single run. Legitimate for scheduled patch/compliance sweeps, but exactly the blast-radius pattern an attacker abusing the automation plane would want.

data_sources.name: AAP job events / API
data_sources.description: Job launch records include the effective host limit and total host count.

detection_logic: Filters job records where limit is empty/null and cross-references the resulting host count against a threshold.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events job_event="playbook_on_start"
| rex field=_raw "host_count=(?<host_count>\d+)"
| rex field=_raw "launched_by=(?<launched_by>\S+)"
| where host_count >= 50
| table _time, job_id, template_name, launched_by, host_count
tuning_guidance: Scheduled compliance/patch jobs are the expected legitimate source; baseline expected schedule and launching accounts, and alert primarily on off-schedule or unfamiliar-launcher occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm the job matches a scheduled/documented fleet-wide operation.
Identify launched_by.
Review the playbook content for destructive tasks.
response_guidance: If unexpected, cancel the job immediately if still running and assess impact across affected hosts.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Job Deploys SSH Authorized Key Across Multiple Hosts
description: Detects a job run whose tasks include the `authorized_key` module (or an equivalent shell-based append to authorized_keys) applied across multiple hosts in a single execution - the automation-plane equivalent of RHEL-017 at fleet scale, and one of the most efficient persistence mechanisms available to an attacker who has compromised AAP.

data_sources.name: AAP job events
data_sources.description: Task action authorized_key, with per-host success count.

detection_logic: Filters job-event records for the authorized_key module and counts distinct hosts affected per job.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events task_action="authorized_key"
| stats dc(host) as hosts_affected values(host) as host_list by job_id, template_name
| where hosts_affected >= 3
tuning_guidance: Legitimate key-rotation automation runs exactly this pattern on a schedule; baseline the expected job template and schedule for authorized SSH key management and alert on any other source.
investigation_steps: Identify the added key's fingerprint and compare against your approved key inventory.
Identify who launched the job.
Check every affected host for the new key and revoke if unauthorized.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, launch a remediation job removing the key from every affected host immediately and rotate the AAP credential used.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1098.004: SSH Authorized Keys

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Job Disables Security Controls Across Multiple Hosts
description: Detects a job run whose tasks stop/disable auditd, SELinux, fapolicyd, or firewalld across multiple hosts in a single execution - the fleet-scale version of the individual RHEL defense-impairment detections, and one of the clearest possible signals of automation-plane abuse for a coordinated attack.

data_sources.name: AAP job events
data_sources.description: Task content/module and result matched against known security-control-impairment patterns, with per-host affected count.

detection_logic: Filters job-event task records whose module/command references auditd, selinux, fapolicyd, or firewalld in a disabling context, and counts distinct affected hosts.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events (task_action="service" OR task_action="systemd" OR task_action="selinux" OR task_action="command")
| where match(_raw, "(?i)(auditd|selinux|fapolicyd|firewalld).*(stop|disable|permissive)")
| stats dc(host) as hosts_affected values(host) as host_list by job_id, template_name
| where hosts_affected >= 3
tuning_guidance: No known legitimate ongoing operational pattern disables these controls fleet-wide except a documented, time-boxed maintenance/troubleshooting window; require explicit change-ticket correlation for any occurrence.
investigation_steps: Identify which control(s) were impaired and on how many hosts.
Identify who launched the job and via what template/credential.
Check for subsequent destructive or persistence activity on the affected hosts (RH-X-010).
response_guidance: Treat as a fleet-wide incident: re-enable controls via emergency automation, rotate the credential used, and investigate the launching account immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Workflow Template Modified to Add a Privileged Node
description: Detects a new node added to a workflow job template that references a privileged job template or credential, silently inserting a powerful step into what may otherwise be a routine, well-reviewed automation chain.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Workflow node creation/association events.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream events for workflow node creation, joined against a lookup of which job templates are considered privileged.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="workflow_job_template_node" operation="create"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "workflow_name=\"(?<workflow_name>[^\"]+)\""
| rex field=_raw "node_template=\"(?<node_template>[^\"]+)\""
| lookup privileged_job_templates.csv node_template OUTPUT is_privileged
| where is_privileged=1
| table _time, actor, workflow_name, node_template
tuning_guidance: Legitimate workflow expansion during a new automation build-out is expected; correlate against a documented change/design review for the workflow.
investigation_steps: Review the new node's position and what triggers it.
Identify actor.
Check whether the workflow has since executed with the new node included.
response_guidance: Remove the unauthorized node if not approved and audit any workflow runs since it was added.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Workflow Approval Node Bypassed or Auto-Approved
description: Detects a workflow approval node being approved by the same account that launched the workflow (self-approval), or approved unusually quickly (seconds) after the workflow reached that node - both patterns suggesting the human-review gate is being rubber-stamped or automated away rather than functioning as intended.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Workflow approval events with the approving user and elapsed time since the node became pending.

detection_logic: Joins the workflow launch event to its subsequent approval event, flagging same-user approval or very short elapsed time.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="workflow_approval" operation="approve"
| rex field=_raw "approved_by=(?<approved_by>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "launched_by=(?<launched_by>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "elapsed_seconds=(?<elapsed_seconds>\d+)"
| where approved_by=launched_by OR elapsed_seconds<=5
| table _time, launched_by, approved_by, elapsed_seconds
tuning_guidance: Some legitimate low-risk workflows are intentionally configured to allow self-approval; scope this detection to workflows explicitly designated as requiring independent review.
investigation_steps: Identify the workflow and what the approval gate was meant to control.
Identify approved_by and launched_by.
Review what the workflow did after approval.
response_guidance: Review the approved change for correctness; tighten the workflow's approval permissions if self-approval should not have been possible.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1548: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Project SCM Source URL Changed
description: Detects a project's SCM source URL being changed - the single highest-leverage software-supply-chain action available in AAP. Every job template referencing the project will subsequently sync and execute playbooks from whatever repository is now configured, potentially attacker-controlled, across every host the templates can reach.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Project update events with the scm_url field.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream project-update events where scm_url changed, comparing the new URL against an approved-source allowlist.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="project" operation="update" "scm_url"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "project_name=\"(?<project_name>[^\"]+)\""
| rex field=_raw "scm_url=\"(?<new_url>[^\"]+)\""
| lookup approved_scm_sources.csv new_url OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, actor, project_name, new_url
tuning_guidance: Legitimate repository migrations (e.g. moving from one Git host to another) are rare, planned events; require every occurrence to correlate with a documented change.
investigation_steps: Compare the new URL against the approved source-control allowlist.
Identify actor.
Check whether a project sync (AAP-018) and subsequent job execution followed immediately - the full RH-X-004 attack chain.
response_guidance: Revert the URL to the approved source immediately if unauthorized, and treat any job execution that occurred after the change as potentially compromised - review and roll back changes made to affected hosts.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Project Synced Immediately Followed by Job Execution
description: Detects a project SCM sync (pulling the latest content from source control) immediately followed by a job launch using that project - confirming that whatever content the sync just pulled in has actually been executed. Combined with AAP-017, this completes the highest-confidence supply-chain attack chain available in AAP.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream / job events
data_sources.description: Project update (sync) events correlated with subsequent job launches referencing the same project.

detection_logic: Joins a project sync completion event to a job launch event referencing the same project within a short window.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="project" operation="update" "status=successful"
| rename _time as sync_time
| rex field=_raw "project_name=\"(?<project_name>[^\"]+)\""
| join type=inner project_name
    [ search index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events job_event="playbook_on_start"
      | rename _time as job_launch_time
      | rex field=_raw "project_name=\"(?<project_name>[^\"]+)\"" ]
| eval delta_seconds=job_launch_time-sync_time
| where delta_seconds>=0 AND delta_seconds<=120
| table sync_time, job_launch_time, project_name, delta_seconds
tuning_guidance: Update-on-launch is a common, legitimate Controller setting (sync-then-run on every job launch); this is high-noise by design unless correlated with an unusual URL change (AAP-017) or unusual launcher/timing.
investigation_steps: Check whether the project's SCM URL changed recently (AAP-017).
Identify who launched the job.
Review the specific playbook content that was pulled and executed.
response_guidance: If the sync source was unauthorized, treat the subsequent job execution as a confirmed compromise and remediate every affected host.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Project Credential Changed
description: Detects the SCM credential attached to a project being changed, which can enable an attacker to redirect the project's pull authentication to an identity they control - useful if the SCM URL itself points at an internal Git server where access is credential-gated rather than URL-gated.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Project update events with a changed credential association.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream project-update events for credential association changes.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="project" operation="update" "credential"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "project_name=\"(?<project_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, project_name
tuning_guidance: Legitimate credential rotation is the expected source; correlate with your SCM credential rotation schedule.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and the new credential.
Confirm the new credential is an approved service identity.
Check subsequent sync/job activity.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and investigate the actor.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Mass Host Addition to an Inventory
description: Detects an unusually large number of hosts added to an inventory in a short window, which can indicate either legitimate bulk fleet onboarding or an attacker expanding an inventory's scope to bring more hosts under a compromised template's future reach.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Host-creation events scoped to a single inventory.

detection_logic: Counts host-creation events per inventory in a rolling window.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="host" operation="create"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "inventory_name=\"(?<inventory_name>[^\"]+)\""
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count as hosts_added by _time, actor, inventory_name
| where hosts_added >= 20
tuning_guidance: Bulk onboarding (new datacenter, new project) is the expected legitimate source; correlate against a documented onboarding project.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and the inventory affected.
Review which job templates target this inventory and their scope.
Confirm the added hosts are legitimate managed systems.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, remove the added hosts and review any job template that might now reach them unexpectedly.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1069: Permission Groups Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Dynamic Inventory Source Modified
description: Detects a change to a dynamic inventory source's configuration (source plugin, credential, or filtering expression). Dynamic inventories automatically populate from cloud/CMDB APIs; a modified source can silently pull in unintended or attacker-controlled hosts on the next sync.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Inventory source update events.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream inventory-source update events.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="inventory_source" operation="update"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "inventory_name=\"(?<inventory_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, inventory_name, _raw
tuning_guidance: Legitimate infrastructure-as-code changes to cloud tagging/filtering criteria are the expected source; correlate against the corresponding cloud-side change.
investigation_steps: Diff the source configuration for the specific change.
Identify actor.
Review the inventory after the next sync for unexpected new hosts.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and audit hosts added by the modified source.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Organization or System Administrator Assigned
description: Detects a user being granted the System Administrator role, or Admin role on an Organization. System Administrators have unrestricted control over every object in Controller including credentials, job templates, and other users' roles - the AAP equivalent of IPA's admins group or RHEL's wheel group.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Role-assignment events.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream role-association events where the granted role is System Administrator or Organization Admin.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream operation="associate" object1="role" (role_name="System Administrator" OR role_name="Admin")
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "target_user=(?<target_user>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, target_user, role_name
tuning_guidance: This should be one of the lowest-volume, highest-scrutiny events in the platform; require every occurrence to tie to a documented, approved access request.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and confirm approval exists.
Review the target account's recent authentication history.
Check what the newly-privileged account does immediately after gaining the role.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized grants immediately and treat both actor and target as potentially compromised.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Team Membership or Role Grant Followed by Privileged Job Launch
description: Detects a user being added to a team or granted execute/admin permission on a job template, followed shortly by that same user launching a privileged job - confirming the newly-granted access was used immediately, which is either efficient legitimate onboarding or a sign the grant itself was the attack.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream / job events
data_sources.description: Role/team grant events correlated with subsequent job-launch events by the same user.

detection_logic: Joins a role/team grant event to a job launch by the same user within a short window.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream operation="associate" object1="role"
| rename _time as grant_time
| rex field=_raw "target_user=(?<user>\S+)"
| join type=inner user
    [ search index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events job_event="playbook_on_start"
      | rename _time as job_launch_time
      | rex field=_raw "launched_by=(?<user>\S+)" ]
| eval delta_minutes=(job_launch_time-grant_time)/60
| where delta_minutes>=0 AND delta_minutes<=30
| table grant_time, job_launch_time, user, delta_minutes
tuning_guidance: Legitimate onboarding often does look exactly like this (grant access, immediately use it for a scheduled task); the value is primarily in surfacing the pairing for review rather than acting as a standalone high-confidence alert.
investigation_steps: Confirm the grant was approved.
Review what the launched job did.
Check whether the granting actor and the job-launching user are the same (self-service) or different (potential collusion/compromise).
response_guidance: No action needed for confirmed legitimate onboarding; escalate if the grant was not approved.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Execution Environment Image Source Changed
description: Detects an Execution Environment's container image reference being changed - the pull source that determines what runtime container actually executes every job that uses it. Pointing at an attacker-controlled or unapproved registry/image is a supply-chain compromise affecting every subsequent job run against that EE.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: ExecutionEnvironment update events with the image field.

detection_logic: Filters activity-stream EE update events, cross-referencing the new image/registry against an approved list.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:activity_stream object1="execution_environment" operation="update" "image"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "ee_name=\"(?<ee_name>[^\"]+)\""
| rex field=_raw "image=\"(?<new_image>[^\"]+)\""
| lookup approved_ee_registries.csv new_image OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, actor, ee_name, new_image
tuning_guidance: Legitimate EE version bumps (pulling a newer tag from the same approved registry) are routine; the allowlist should match on registry/repository rather than exact tag to keep noise low.
investigation_steps: Compare the new image reference against the approved registry list.
Identify actor.
Check for job runs against the EE since the change and review their behavior.
response_guidance: Revert to an approved image immediately if unauthorized, and treat any job that ran under the unapproved EE as potentially compromised.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Execution Environment Using 'latest' Tag Where Pinned Versions Are Required
description: Detects an Execution Environment configured to pull the `:latest` tag rather than a pinned, version-specific image reference, in an environment where policy requires pinned versions. Using `latest` means the exact code that runs can change silently on the next pull without any corresponding AAP-side configuration change to review.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream / configuration scan
data_sources.description: EE image field content.

detection_logic: Scans configured EE image references for a missing or ':latest' tag.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:config_scan:execution_environments (image="*:latest" OR NOT image="*:*")
| table _time, ee_name, image
tuning_guidance: Some non-production/sandbox EEs may intentionally track latest; scope this policy check to production-tier EEs only.
investigation_steps: Identify which job templates use this EE.
Check the image's actual current digest against what was last reviewed/approved.
Pin to a specific digest or version tag.
response_guidance: Remediate as a hardening finding; treat as higher urgency if paired with an unexpected image-source change (AAP-024).
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Collection Uploaded to a Namespace
description: Detects a new Ansible Collection version being uploaded to Automation Hub (public or private). Collections bundle modules, roles, and plugins that execute with the same privilege as any other automation content; a malicious collection is a direct code-execution supply-chain vector into every playbook that imports it.

techniques.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

data_sources.name: Automation Hub API log
data_sources.description: Collection upload events with the uploading user, namespace, and version.

detection_logic: Filters Hub API logs for collection artifact upload events.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=hub:api_access method="POST" path="*/artifacts/collections/*"
| rex field=_raw "user=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "namespace=(?<namespace>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, namespace, _raw
tuning_guidance: Legitimate internal collection development and publishing is expected in namespaces owned by platform/automation teams; scrutinize uploads to namespaces the actor does not normally publish to, and any upload from an unfamiliar account.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and their normal publishing history.
Review the collection's content (plugins, roles, module code) for anything unexpected.
Check whether the collection has been approved/certified before any job template references it.
response_guidance: Quarantine unreviewed/unexpected collections before they reach an approved repository, and investigate the uploading account.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.001: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Collection Approved/Published to the Certified Repository
description: Detects a collection version being moved from the staging/rejected repository into the approved/published (certified) repository, making it available for use by every project and job template in the platform. The approval step is meant to be a human-review gate; its bypass or rubber-stamping is the point where a supply-chain-compromised collection becomes usable fleet-wide.

techniques.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

data_sources.name: Automation Hub API log
data_sources.description: Repository move/approval events.

detection_logic: Filters Hub API logs for repository-move operations targeting the published/certified repository.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=hub:api_access "move" "published"
| rex field=_raw "user=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "collection=(?<collection_name>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, collection_name
tuning_guidance: Correlate approval timing against the initial upload (AAP-026) - a near-instant approval by the same account that uploaded it (self-approval of a brand-new, unreviewed collection) is far higher-suspicion than a delayed approval by a different, designated reviewer.
investigation_steps: Confirm the approving actor is a designated content reviewer, not the uploader.
Review whatever security scanning was run against the collection prior to approval.
Check for job templates that started using the collection immediately after approval.
response_guidance: If approval was improper, revert the collection to staging/rejected immediately and audit any job execution that already used it.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.001: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Collection Namespace Ownership Changed
description: Detects a change to who is authorized to publish under a given collection namespace. An attacker who adds themselves as a namespace owner can subsequently publish malicious updates to an already-trusted, widely-used collection name without needing to trick anyone into approving a brand-new namespace.

data_sources.name: Automation Hub API log
data_sources.description: Namespace owner-list modification events.

detection_logic: Filters Hub API logs for namespace owner-list updates.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=hub:api_access "PATCH" "*/namespaces/*"
| rex field=_raw "user=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "namespace=(?<namespace>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, namespace
tuning_guidance: Rare, deliberate team-membership changes are the expected source; require change-ticket correlation for any namespace with widely-used, trusted collections.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and the namespace's collection usage footprint (how many projects depend on it).
Confirm the ownership change was approved.
Watch for a subsequent collection upload from the newly-added owner.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized ownership changes and audit any content published under the namespace since the change.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Rulebook Activation Created
description: Detects a new EDA rulebook activation being created - a standing, always-on process that automatically launches automation in response to incoming events. Because activations run continuously and trigger without a human explicitly launching each job, a malicious rulebook is a durable, low-visibility persistence and execution mechanism.

data_sources.name: AAP EDA activity log
data_sources.description: Rulebook activation creation events.

detection_logic: Filters EDA activity logs for activation-creation events.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:eda_activity operation="create" object="activation"
| rex field=_raw "actor=(?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "rulebook_name=\"(?<rulebook_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, rulebook_name
tuning_guidance: Legitimate EDA adoption for new automated-remediation use cases is expected during platform rollout; correlate against a documented use-case design/review.
investigation_steps: Review the rulebook's event source and the action(s) it triggers.
Identify actor.
Check what job template/action the rulebook is wired to and its privilege level.
response_guidance: Disable the activation if unauthorized and review any actions it has already triggered.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1546: Event Triggered Execution

author: Threat Detection Library

title: EDA Rulebook Triggers Privileged Automation
description: Detects an EDA rulebook activation wired to a job template that runs with privilege escalation enabled or targets a broad inventory. Combined with an attacker-controlled or spoofable event source, this creates a persistent trigger for fleet-wide privileged execution that requires no further interactive access once established.

data_sources.name: AAP EDA activity log
data_sources.description: Activation configuration showing the linked job template.

detection_logic: Cross-references EDA activation configuration against the privileged-job-template lookup used in AAP-015.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:eda_activity object="activation"
| rex field=_raw "rulebook_name=\"(?<rulebook_name>[^\"]+)\""
| rex field=_raw "linked_template=\"(?<linked_template>[^\"]+)\""
| lookup privileged_job_templates.csv linked_template OUTPUT is_privileged
| where is_privileged=1
| table _time, rulebook_name, linked_template
tuning_guidance: Legitimate automated-remediation use cases (auto-restart a failed service, auto-scale) may genuinely need privileged execution; require these to use the narrowest possible job template scope and a tightly-controlled event source rather than suppressing the finding.
investigation_steps: Review the event source configuration for how easily it could be spoofed/triggered by an untrusted party.
Review the linked template's actual scope and privilege.
Check the activation's trigger history for unexpected firings.
response_guidance: Narrow the linked template's scope/privilege or harden the event source if the risk is not justified by the use case.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1546: Event Triggered Execution

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Event Storm Triggering Repeated Automation Execution
description: Detects an unusually high rate of event-triggered job launches from a single EDA activation in a short window, which can indicate either a malfunctioning/looping event source or an attacker deliberately flooding an event source to trigger repeated automation execution as a denial-of-service or resource-exhaustion technique.

data_sources.name: AAP EDA activity log / job events
data_sources.description: Job-launch volume attributed to a single activation.

detection_logic: Counts job launches per EDA activation in a rolling window.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=aap:eda_activity object="job_launch"
| rex field=_raw "rulebook_name=\"(?<rulebook_name>[^\"]+)\""
| bin _time span=5m
| stats count as launch_count by _time, rulebook_name
| where launch_count >= 30
tuning_guidance: A genuinely bursty but legitimate event source (e.g. a bulk monitoring alert flood during a real outage) can trigger this; correlate against known infrastructure incidents before treating as adversarial.
investigation_steps: Identify the event source and whether it is behaving normally.
Review the resource impact of the repeated executions on target hosts and the Controller itself.
Check whether the event source could have been externally triggered/spoofed.
response_guidance: Pause the activation if it is causing operational impact, and harden the event source (authentication, rate limiting) if it was externally triggerable.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Endpoint Denial of Service

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Receptor Node or Peer Added to the Mesh
description: Detects a new node joining the receptor mesh (which routes job execution work between Controller and execution/hop nodes). A rogue receptor node, once trusted by the mesh, can potentially receive or observe routed job execution traffic and present itself as a legitimate execution target.

data_sources.name: receptor logs
data_sources.description: Node connection/peer events.

detection_logic: Monitors receptor's connection log for new peer/node-id entries not present in the last-known topology snapshot.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=receptor_log "connection established" OR "new node"
| rex field=_raw "node_id=(?<node_id>\S+)"
| lookup known_receptor_topology.csv node_id OUTPUT is_known
| where isnull(is_known)
| table _time, node_id, _raw
tuning_guidance: Planned scale-out of execution capacity is the expected legitimate source and should follow a documented infrastructure change process.
investigation_steps: Confirm the new node is an approved, hardened execution host under IT control.
Review its issued certificate/identity.
Check what job traffic has routed through it since joining.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized nodes from the mesh immediately and rotate mesh certificates if compromise is suspected.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Receptor Service Impaired or Certificate Changed
description: Detects the receptor service being stopped, or its TLS certificate being replaced. Because receptor carries all job-execution traffic across the automation mesh, its impairment can disrupt fleet management entirely, while a certificate replacement could facilitate a mesh man-in-the-middle if not tightly controlled.

data_sources.name: receptor logs / systemd
data_sources.description: Service state-change and certificate-reload events.

detection_logic: Matches systemd service-stop events for the receptor unit and certificate-reload log lines.
spl:
index=aap sourcetype=receptor_log ("service stopped" OR "certificate reloaded" OR "TLS configuration changed")
| table _time, host, _raw
tuning_guidance: Planned certificate rotation and maintenance windows are the expected legitimate sources; correlate with a change ticket.
investigation_steps: Identify what changed and on which node.
Check whether job routing was disrupted as a result.
Verify the new certificate's issuer/chain if this was a certificate change.
response_guidance: Restore service/certificate configuration immediately if unauthorized and investigate the change.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Repeated Satellite Login Failures
description: Detects a burst of failed login attempts against the Satellite web UI or API for a single user or source. Satellite governs software content and remote execution for the entire RHEL fleet, making its authentication surface a high-value brute-force target.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Authentication attempts with outcome, username, and source IP.

detection_logic: Counts failed login events per user/source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "Failed login" OR "Authentication failure"
| rex field=_raw "for user '(?<user>[^']+)'.*from (?<src_ip>[\d\.:]+)"
| bin _time span=5m
| stats count as failures by _time, user, src_ip
| where failures >= 8
tuning_guidance: A CI/CD pipeline or Hammer CLI script using a stale credential will retry and fail repeatedly; fix the offending automation rather than suppressing broadly.
investigation_steps: Identify src_ip.
Check for a subsequent successful login (SAT-002).
Check whether multiple accounts are targeted from the same source.
response_guidance: Lock the account after continued failures and investigate/block the source.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful Satellite Login Following Repeated Failures
description: Detects a successful Satellite authentication for a user/source pair that recently produced multiple failures - a compromised-credential indicator on a platform that can push content and execute remote commands across the entire managed RHEL estate.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Correlates failed and successful login events for the same user/source.

detection_logic: Joins a successful login to a preceding burst of failures for the same user/source within a short window.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "Successful login for user"
| rex field=_raw "for user '(?<user>[^']+)'.*from (?<src_ip>[\d\.:]+)"
| rename _time as success_time
| join type=inner user, src_ip
    [ search index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "Failed login"
      | rex field=_raw "for user '(?<user>[^']+)'.*from (?<src_ip>[\d\.:]+)"
      | bin _time span=15m
      | stats count as prior_failures by _time, user, src_ip
      | where prior_failures >= 5 ]
| table success_time, user, src_ip, prior_failures
tuning_guidance: Rare for legitimate human logins; tune per your typical mistyped-password rate.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the account owner whether expected.
Review what the account has permission to do (content, remote execution, host management).
Review activity performed since the login.
response_guidance: Treat as a likely-compromised account: disable it, and audit every content/remote-execution action taken under it.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unusual Hammer CLI Usage Pattern
description: Detects an unusually high volume of Hammer CLI (Satellite's command-line client) API calls from a single session, or use of subcommands rarely invoked interactively (bulk host operations, content-view publish, activation-key modification), consistent with scripted abuse of a compromised admin session.

data_sources.name: Foreman API access log
data_sources.description: Per-session API call volume and subcommand/endpoint pattern.

detection_logic: Counts distinct API calls per user/session in a rolling window and flags high-risk endpoint categories specifically.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:api_access
| bin _time span=5m
| stats count as call_count dc(path) as distinct_endpoints by _time, user
| where call_count >= 100
tuning_guidance: Legitimate automation/orchestration scripts using Hammer or the API directly are the primary source; allowlist known automation accounts and focus this detection on interactive human sessions.
investigation_steps: Identify the user and session origin.
Review the specific endpoints/subcommands invoked.
Confirm whether this matches a documented bulk-operation task.
response_guidance: Investigate if unexplained; no action needed for confirmed legitimate automation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Satellite Administrator Created
description: Detects a user being granted the Administrator role in Satellite. Satellite admins control content distribution, remote execution, and provisioning for the entire fleet - compromise here is functionally equivalent to compromising the software supply chain and command-execution channel for every managed RHEL host.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Role-assignment audit events.

detection_logic: Filters audit records for role-assignment operations granting the Administrator role.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "role" "Administrator" ("assigned" OR "added")
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "to (?<target_user>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, target_user
tuning_guidance: This should be a rare, deliberate, fully-approved action; require documented approval for every occurrence.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and confirm approval.
Review the target account's recent authentication history.
Check for content/remote-execution actions immediately after the grant.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized grants immediately and treat both accounts as potentially compromised.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Organization or Location Scope Widened for a Role
description: Detects a role or permission filter's organization/location scope being widened, expanding which hosts and content a role's members can act upon without necessarily changing the role's permission set itself - a subtler privilege-expansion path than an outright Administrator grant.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Role/filter scope-modification events.

detection_logic: Filters audit records for filter-taxonomy (organization/location) modification on existing roles.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "filter" ("organization_ids" OR "location_ids") "updated"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "role=(?<role_name>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, role_name
tuning_guidance: Legitimate organizational restructuring (new business unit onboarding) is the expected source; correlate against a documented reorg.
investigation_steps: Identify the scope change and affected role's membership.
Identify actor.
Review what those members subsequently accessed.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized and audit access exercised under the expanded scope.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Repository URL Changed
description: Detects a repository's upstream URL being changed. Every content view built from this repository will subsequently sync and distribute packages from whatever source is now configured - the single highest-leverage software-supply-chain action available in Satellite, analogous to AAP-017 for the automation plane.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Repository update events with the url field.

detection_logic: Filters repository-update audit records where the URL changed, checked against an approved-source allowlist.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "repository" "url" "updated"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "repo=(?<repo_name>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "url=\"(?<new_url>[^\"]+)\""
| lookup approved_repo_sources.csv new_url OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, actor, repo_name, new_url
tuning_guidance: Legitimate mirror migrations are rare, planned events; require every occurrence to correlate with a documented change.
investigation_steps: Compare the new URL against the approved-source allowlist.
Identify actor.
Check whether a sync (SAT-007) and content view publish followed - the full RH-X-006 attack chain.
response_guidance: Revert the URL immediately if unauthorized and treat any content synced from it as compromised until proven otherwise - do not promote it to production.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPG Signature Verification Weakened or Disabled
description: Detects a repository's GPG-check requirement being disabled, or its trusted GPG key being changed/removed. GPG verification is the primary integrity control preventing tampered or unsigned RPM content from being trusted; disabling it removes the last line of defense against a compromised upstream mirror.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Repository gpg_key_id / unprotected field changes.

detection_logic: Filters repository-update events where gpgcheck transitions to false or the gpg_key_id is cleared/changed.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "repository" ("gpgcheck=false" OR "gpg_key" "removed")
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "repo=(?<repo_name>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, repo_name
tuning_guidance: Very rare legitimate need (some internal/dev repositories intentionally ship unsigned packages); require these to be explicitly non-production repositories only.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and the repository's production usage.
Check for content sync immediately after.
Verify package signatures manually for anything synced while unprotected.
response_guidance: Re-enable GPG checking immediately, and treat any package synced while disabled as untrusted pending manual verification.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1553: Subvert Trust Controls

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Unexpected Repository Synchronization
description: Detects a repository sync task launching shortly after its URL or GPG configuration changed - confirming that whatever new/unprotected source was just configured has actually been pulled in. Combined with SAT-006/SAT-007, this completes the highest-confidence Satellite supply-chain attack chain.

data_sources.name: Foreman/Pulp task log
data_sources.description: Repository sync task events correlated with the preceding configuration change.

detection_logic: Joins a repository configuration change to a subsequent sync task for the same repository within a short window.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "repository" "updated"
| rename _time as config_change_time
| rex field=_raw "repo=(?<repo_name>\S+)"
| join type=inner repo_name
    [ search index=satellite sourcetype=pulp:task "sync" "completed"
      | rename _time as sync_time
      | rex field=_raw "repo=(?<repo_name>\S+)" ]
| eval delta_minutes=(sync_time-config_change_time)/60
| where delta_minutes>=0 AND delta_minutes<=60
| table config_change_time, sync_time, repo_name, delta_minutes
tuning_guidance: Scheduled syncs happen regardless of recent config changes; this is most valuable specifically when paired with an unapproved URL/GPG change (SAT-006/SAT-007) rather than as a standalone signal.
investigation_steps: Check whether the preceding config change was authorized.
Review what packages were pulled in by the sync.
Check whether a content view was published/promoted using the newly-synced content (RH-X-006).
response_guidance: If the preceding change was unauthorized, do not promote the synced content and roll back the repository configuration immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Content View Filter Weakened
description: Detects a content view's package filter being removed or widened (e.g. an include-list narrowed filter replaced with an exclude-list that lets everything through). Content view filters are a key control for ensuring only vetted, approved packages reach production; weakening them allows arbitrary upstream content to flow through on the next publish.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Content view filter update events.

detection_logic: Filters content-view-filter update/delete audit records.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "content_view_filter" ("updated" OR "destroyed")
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "content_view=(?<cv_name>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, cv_name, _raw
tuning_guidance: Legitimate package-catalog expansion for a new application requirement is the expected source; correlate against a documented package-approval request.
investigation_steps: Diff the filter's rule set for what was removed/widened.
Identify actor.
Check what new packages entered the content view on the next publish.
response_guidance: Restore the filter if unauthorized before the next publish/promotion.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1553: Subvert Trust Controls

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Content View Published or Promoted Outside Change Window
description: Detects a content view publish or lifecycle-environment promotion occurring outside documented maintenance/change windows, which can indicate either an operational process breakdown or an attacker pushing compromised content while off-hours activity is less likely to be reviewed in real time.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Content view publish/promote task events with timestamp.

detection_logic: Filters publish/promote events and cross-references the event timestamp against a documented change-window schedule.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production ("content_view" "publish") OR ("content_view" "promote")
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "content_view=(?<cv_name>\S+)"
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| where hour<6 OR hour>20
| table _time, actor, cv_name, hour
tuning_guidance: Global/follow-the-sun operations teams may have legitimately different 'normal hours'; scope the window to your actual change-management policy rather than a single timezone assumption.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether an emergency change ticket covers this action.
Identify actor.
Review what changed in the published content.
response_guidance: No action for a documented emergency change; investigate and potentially roll back for an undocumented one.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Rapid Promotion Through Multiple Lifecycle Environments
description: Detects a content view version being promoted through several lifecycle environments (e.g. Dev -> Test -> Production) in rapid succession, skipping the soak/validation time each stage is meant to provide. This is the Satellite-specific version of bypassing a staged rollout, and is exactly the pattern an attacker would use to rush compromised content into production before anyone notices something is wrong at an earlier stage.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Promotion events for a content view version across environments, with timestamps.

detection_logic: Counts distinct lifecycle environments a single content view version is promoted into within a short window.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "content_view_version" "promote"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "content_view=(?<cv_name>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "version=(?<cv_version>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "environment=(?<environment>\S+)"
| bin _time span=30m
| stats dc(environment) as environments_touched values(environment) as environment_list by _time, actor, cv_name, cv_version
| where environments_touched >= 3
tuning_guidance: Emergency security-patch rollouts legitimately fast-track promotion; require these to be tied to a documented emergency-change process (e.g. a CVE remediation ticket).
investigation_steps: Confirm an emergency change justifies the rapid promotion.
Identify actor.
Review exactly what package/errata changes were included in the promoted version.
response_guidance: If undocumented, halt further promotion, review the content thoroughly before it reaches additional hosts, and consider reverting production if already promoted.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Direct Promotion to Production Lifecycle Environment
description: Detects a content view version being promoted directly into the Production lifecycle environment without having first passed through the intermediate (Dev/Test/QA) environments defined in the lifecycle path - bypassing every validation stage designed to catch a problem, malicious or otherwise, before it reaches live systems.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Promotion events showing the source and destination environment for a version.

detection_logic: Checks whether a version being promoted to Production has a promotion history including the environment(s) immediately preceding it in the defined lifecycle path; flags a skip.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "content_view_version" "promote" environment="Production"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "content_view=(?<cv_name>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "version=(?<cv_version>\S+)"
| lookup cv_promotion_history.csv cv_name, cv_version OUTPUT prior_environments
| where NOT match(prior_environments, "QA|Test")
| table _time, actor, cv_name, cv_version, prior_environments
tuning_guidance: A documented emergency-change process for critical security patches is the only expected legitimate source; require formal sign-off for any occurrence.
investigation_steps: Confirm emergency-change approval.
Review the version's full content diff against what is currently in Production.
Identify actor.
response_guidance: If undocumented, treat as a high-priority incident - review the promoted content immediately and be prepared to roll back.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002: Compromise Software Supply Chain

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Activation Key Host Limit or Subscription Scope Changed
description: Detects an activation key's host limit being increased/removed or its associated content view/lifecycle environment changed. Activation keys govern what content and configuration a newly-registered host receives; a broadened key can be used to register many more (or differently-configured) hosts than intended.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Activation key update events.

detection_logic: Filters activation-key update audit records.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "activation_key" "updated"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "name=(?<key_name>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, key_name, _raw
tuning_guidance: Legitimate fleet-growth planning changes host limits periodically; correlate against a documented capacity-planning change.
investigation_steps: Identify what specifically changed (limit, content view, environment).
Identify actor.
Check for a burst of new host registrations using the key immediately after (SAT-014).
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes and review any new registrations that occurred under the modified key.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Mass Host Registration Using a Single Activation Key
description: Detects an unusually high number of new host registrations against a single activation key in a short window, which can indicate either legitimate bulk provisioning (a new datacenter/cluster build-out) or an attacker using a leaked/overly-broad activation key to enroll rogue systems into the managed fleet's content and configuration scope.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Host registration events with the activation key used.

detection_logic: Counts host-registration events per activation key in a rolling window.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "host registered" "activation_key"
| rex field=_raw "activation_key=(?<key_name>\S+)"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats count as hosts_registered values(host) as host_list by _time, key_name
| where hosts_registered >= 25
tuning_guidance: Bulk provisioning during planned infrastructure build-outs is the expected legitimate source; correlate against a documented provisioning project and its expected host count.
investigation_steps: Identify the source(s) of the registration requests.
Confirm the newly-registered hosts are legitimate, expected systems.
Review what content/configuration they received via the key.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, revoke/rotate the activation key and investigate/deregister the rogue hosts.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Mass Host Deregistration/Deletion
description: Detects a burst of host deregistrations or deletions from Satellite's inventory in a short window, removing hosts from centralized management/patching/compliance visibility - either an operational bulk-decommission or an attacker attempting to blind the management plane to a set of compromised hosts.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Host deletion/unregister events.

detection_logic: Counts host-deletion events by actor in a rolling window.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "host" ("destroyed" OR "unregistered")
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| bin _time span=15m
| stats count as hosts_removed values(host) as host_list by _time, actor
| where hosts_removed >= 10
tuning_guidance: Planned fleet decommissioning is the expected legitimate source; correlate against a documented decommission project and its expected host list.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and the specific hosts removed.
Confirm each host is genuinely being decommissioned (not still in active production use).
Check whether removal coincides with other suspicious activity on those hosts (RH-X-010).
response_guidance: If unauthorized, this is a P1 - the removed hosts may be actively compromised and hidden from management visibility; investigate them directly via other means immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Provisioning Template Modified
description: Detects a provisioning (kickstart/PXE) template being modified. Every new host built using the template inherits whatever it contains - a compromised template can inject a backdoor account, an SSH key, or a malicious post-install script into every future system built from it, silently and durably.

techniques.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Provisioning template update events.

detection_logic: Filters provisioning-template update audit records.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "provisioning_template" "updated"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "name=\"(?<template_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, template_name
tuning_guidance: Legitimate template maintenance (new OS version support, hardening updates) is the expected source; require peer review/change-ticket correlation for production-tier templates.
investigation_steps: Diff the template content, focusing on %post sections, root password/SSH key configuration, and any added packages or firstboot scripts.
Identify actor.
Check for any hosts already built using the modified template.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately and rebuild/audit any host provisioned with the compromised template.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.001: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Satellite Remote Execution Job Launched
description: Detects a Remote Execution (REX) job being launched from Satellite. REX runs arbitrary shell commands/scripts across selected hosts via SSH from the Satellite/Capsule server, making it functionally equivalent in impact to AAP job execution and one of the highest-value capabilities an attacker could gain from a compromised Satellite account.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log / REX job log
data_sources.description: Job invocation records with launching user, target hosts, and command/script.

detection_logic: Filters audit records for remote_execution job creation.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "job_invocation" "create"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "job_id=(?<job_id>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, job_id, _raw
tuning_guidance: Routine patch/config-management REX jobs are common and expected; the value is in the full audit trail feeding the higher-severity building-block detections below (SAT-018 through SAT-020).
investigation_steps: Identify actor, target hosts, and the exact command/script.
Confirm against a maintenance schedule if applicable.
Review job output/results for unexpected behavior.
response_guidance: No standalone action for routine, approved jobs; escalate per the correlated detections for high-risk command patterns.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Remote Execution Job Runs as root Against Many Hosts
description: Detects a Remote Execution job configured to run as root and targeting a large number of hosts in a single invocation - the Satellite-specific version of the AAP-012 fleet-wide-blast-radius pattern, and among the most consequential single actions available to a Satellite user.

data_sources.name: REX job log
data_sources.description: Job invocation records with effective_user and target host count.

detection_logic: Filters job-invocation records where effective_user=root and host_count exceeds a threshold.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "job_invocation" effective_user="root"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "host_count=(?<host_count>\d+)"
| where host_count >= 25
| table _time, actor, job_id, host_count
tuning_guidance: Scheduled fleet-wide patch/compliance jobs are the expected legitimate source; baseline the expected schedule and launching accounts.
investigation_steps: Confirm the job matches a scheduled/documented operation.
Review the exact command/script for destructive potential.
Identify actor.
response_guidance: If unexpected, attempt to cancel the job if still running and assess impact across targeted hosts immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Remote Execution Job Contains Security-Control-Impairment Commands
description: Detects a Remote Execution job whose command/script content stops or disables auditd, SELinux, fapolicyd, or firewalld - the Satellite-specific version of AAP-014, and an equally clear signal of management-plane abuse for a coordinated attack.

data_sources.name: REX job log
data_sources.description: Job command/script content matched against known security-control-impairment patterns.

detection_logic: Matches job command/script content for auditd/SELinux/fapolicyd/firewalld disabling patterns.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "job_invocation" "create"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "command=\"(?<command>[^\"]+)\""
| where match(command, "(?i)(auditd|selinux|fapolicyd|firewalld).*(stop|disable|permissive)")
| table _time, actor, command
tuning_guidance: No known legitimate ongoing operational pattern disables these controls fleet-wide except a documented, time-boxed maintenance window; require explicit change-ticket correlation for any occurrence.
investigation_steps: Identify which control(s) were targeted and on how many hosts.
Identify actor.
Check for subsequent destructive or persistence activity on affected hosts.
response_guidance: Treat as a fleet-wide incident: re-enable controls via emergency remote execution, and investigate the launching account immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1072: Software Deployment Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Remote Execution Job Contains Destructive Command Pattern
description: Detects a Remote Execution job whose command/script content matches known destructive patterns - mass file deletion, disk-wipe utilities, or ransomware-like encryption commands - targeting potentially many hosts simultaneously through the management plane.

data_sources.name: REX job log
data_sources.description: Job command/script content matched against destructive command patterns.

detection_logic: Matches job command/script content against destructive-command signatures (rm -rf /, shred, wipefs, dd to a block device, openssl-based mass encryption one-liners).
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "job_invocation" "create"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "command=\"(?<command>[^\"]+)\""
| where match(command, "(?i)(rm\s+-rf\s+/|shred\s|wipefs\s|of=/dev/(sd|nvme|vd)|openssl\s+enc.*-in\s+/)")
| table _time, actor, command
tuning_guidance: Essentially zero legitimate false-positive source for this specific pattern set at fleet scale; treat as page-now.
investigation_steps: Identify targeted hosts and immediately assess whether the job has already executed.
Identify actor.
If still pending/running, attempt emergency cancellation.
response_guidance: Treat as an active, fleet-wide destructive attack: cancel the job immediately if possible, isolate affected hosts, and engage incident response at the highest priority.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1486: Data Encrypted for Impact

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Capsule Server Registered
description: Detects a new Capsule server being registered to Satellite. A Capsule proxies content distribution, DNS/DHCP, and remote execution for a segment of the fleet (often a remote site); a rogue Capsule can intercept or manipulate content/commands for every host that registers through it.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Capsule (smart_proxy) registration events.

detection_logic: Filters audit records for smart_proxy creation.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "smart_proxy" "created"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "name=\"(?<capsule_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, capsule_name
tuning_guidance: Planned site/DR expansion is the only expected legitimate source and should follow a documented infrastructure change process.
investigation_steps: Confirm the new Capsule host is approved, hardened infrastructure under IT control.
Identify actor.
Review its certificate and the features (content, DNS, DHCP, REX) it was granted.
response_guidance: Remove an unauthorized Capsule immediately and treat any host that registered through it as potentially compromised.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Capsule Certificate Replaced
description: Detects a Capsule's TLS certificate being replaced/re-signed. Legitimate during scheduled certificate rotation, but an unexpected replacement could indicate an attacker attempting to interpose a rogue Capsule identity or facilitate content/command interception via a substituted trust anchor.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Capsule certificate regeneration/registration events.

detection_logic: Filters audit records for Capsule certificate refresh operations.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "smart_proxy" "certificate" "refresh"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "name=\"(?<capsule_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, actor, capsule_name
tuning_guidance: Scheduled certificate rotation (annual renewal) is the expected legitimate source; correlate against the documented rotation schedule.
investigation_steps: Confirm the rotation was scheduled.
Identify actor.
Verify the new certificate's chain of trust back to the Satellite CA.
response_guidance: If unexpected, treat as a potential Capsule-identity compromise and investigate immediately.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1553: Subvert Trust Controls

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Capsule Synchronization Failure or Unexpected Communication Pattern
description: Detects a Capsule reporting sync errors or unexpected communication timing with the parent Satellite server, which can indicate a legitimate network/operational issue or tampering with the Capsule's configuration/connectivity as a precursor to operating it outside central oversight.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Capsule sync status and error records.

detection_logic: Filters Capsule sync-status records for error/failure states, with attention to sustained (not transient) failures.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "smart_proxy" "sync" ("error" OR "failed")
