| rex field=_raw "name=\"(?<capsule_name>[^\"]+)\""
| table _time, capsule_name, _raw
tuning_guidance: Transient network issues cause brief sync errors regularly; escalate specifically on sustained failures beyond the normal sync interval.
investigation_steps: Identify the specific Capsule and error condition.
Check for corresponding network/infrastructure incidents.
Verify the Capsule's configuration has not been tampered with.
response_guidance: Resolve the underlying issue; investigate for tampering if the failure pattern is unexplained by infrastructure issues.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1082: System Information Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Content Uploaded Directly to Pulp Outside Satellite Workflow
description: Detects content (RPM, container image, file) being uploaded directly via the Pulp API rather than through Satellite's normal repository-sync workflow. Because Pulp is the actual content-storage backend beneath Satellite, direct API access bypasses Satellite-layer approval/audit controls entirely.

techniques.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

data_sources.name: Pulp API log
data_sources.description: Content upload/import API calls with the authenticated identity.

detection_logic: Filters Pulp API logs for content-upload endpoints, cross-referenced against known Satellite service-account callers to isolate direct/out-of-band access.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=pulp:api_access method="POST" path="*/content/*/upload/*"
| rex field=_raw "user=(?<actor>\S+)"
| lookup satellite_service_accounts.csv actor OUTPUT is_satellite_service
| where isnull(is_satellite_service)
| table _time, actor, path
tuning_guidance: Satellite's own backend service account performs the vast majority of legitimate Pulp API traffic; any direct human/other-account access is inherently unusual and worth reviewing.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and the uploaded content.
Determine whether this bypassed Satellite's normal approval workflow entirely.
Check whether the content subsequently appeared in a repository/content view.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized content immediately and investigate how direct Pulp API access was obtained.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.001: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Pulp Content Deleted in Bulk
description: Detects a large number of content units (packages, images) being deleted from Pulp storage in a short window, which can disrupt the entire content-distribution pipeline for the fleet and inhibit the ability to reinstall/roll back software during incident recovery.

data_sources.name: Pulp API log
data_sources.description: Content deletion API call volume.

detection_logic: Counts content-deletion API calls per actor in a rolling window.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=pulp:api_access method="DELETE" path="*/content/*"
| rex field=_raw "user=(?<actor>\S+)"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count as deletion_count by _time, actor
| where deletion_count >= 100
tuning_guidance: Scheduled orphan-content cleanup (a routine Satellite maintenance task) is the expected legitimate source; exclude the known cleanup service account.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and what was deleted.
Confirm this matches the routine cleanup schedule and account.
Assess impact on content availability for the fleet.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, assess whether content can be re-synced from upstream and investigate the actor.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: per actor, excluding known cleanup service account

title: Kickstart Root Password or SSH Key Configuration Changed
description: Detects a change to the root password hash or injected SSH authorized key referenced by a kickstart/provisioning template or host group. Every host subsequently built inherits this credential material - an attacker-controlled root password or key here grants durable access to the entire future fleet built from that template.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Host group / provisioning parameter update events for root_pass and ssh authorized keys.

detection_logic: Filters parameter/host-group update audit records for root_pass or ssh key-related parameters.
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "parameter" ("root_pass" OR "ssh_authorized_key") "updated"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "target=(?<target_name>\S+)"
| table _time, actor, target_name
tuning_guidance: Legitimate credential rotation for the default build-time root password is expected periodically; correlate against your documented rotation schedule.
investigation_steps: Identify actor and target (global default vs. a specific host group/template).
Confirm the change matches an approved rotation.
Check for any hosts already built using the modified value.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately and rebuild/re-key any host provisioned with the compromised credential.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1098.004: SSH Authorized Keys

author: Threat Detection Library

title: PXE/Kickstart Post-Install Script Modified
description: Detects a change to a provisioning template's %post section (the script executed at the end of OS installation, with root privilege, before the host is ever handed to its owner). Modifying this section is one of the most powerful supply-chain footholds available in Satellite - it runs unconditionally, as root, on every new host, before any other security control (SELinux policy, auditd, fapolicyd) has even started.

data_sources.name: Foreman production log
data_sources.description: Provisioning template content update events, specifically diffing the %post section.

detection_logic: Filters provisioning-template updates and flags changes touching the %post section specifically (requires diffing template content, not just detecting any update).
spl:
index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "provisioning_template" "updated"
| rex field=_raw "by (?<actor>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "name=\"(?<template_name>[^\"]+)\""
| lookup template_post_section_hash.csv template_name OUTPUT prior_post_hash
| eval current_post_hash=md5(_raw)
| where current_post_hash!=prior_post_hash
| table _time, actor, template_name
tuning_guidance: Legitimate post-install automation changes (adding a new baseline package, a new monitoring agent) are the expected source; require peer review for any %post change on production-tier templates.
investigation_steps: Diff the exact %post content change.
Identify actor.
Immediately audit any host already built since the change for the new script's effects.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized changes immediately; treat every host provisioned since the change as potentially compromised and rebuild from known-good media if warranted.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: IPA Privileged Identity Compromise Followed by RHEL SSH Access
description: Correlates a likely-compromised IPA principal (IPA-002: successful Kerberos auth following repeated failures, or IPA-004: admin login from an unusual source) with a subsequent SSH session on a RHEL host authenticated via that same principal's Kerberos/SSSD identity, followed by sudo or root activity on the target. This is the canonical identity-to-endpoint attack chain in a Red Hat environment: RHEL alone shows only 'a normal SSH login and some sudo commands,' which looks unremarkable without the preceding IPA-side compromise signal for context.

data_sources.name: krb5kdc + RHEL sshd/sudo
data_sources.description: Correlates a KDC-side compromise indicator with client-side SSH/sudo activity for the same principal.

detection_logic: Joins IPA-002/IPA-004 events to a subsequent SSH acceptance on any RHEL host for the same principal within a short window, then to any sudo/root activity in that session.
spl:
`comment("Stage 1: pull already-flagged IPA compromise events (from IPA-002 / IPA-004 saved searches)")`
| savedsearch "IPA-002_successful_auth_after_failures"
| append [ savedsearch "IPA-004_admin_login_unusual_source" ]
| rename _time as compromise_time
| join type=inner principal
    [ search index=linux sourcetype=linux_secure "Accepted"
      | rex field=_raw "Accepted \S+ for (?<principal>\S+) from"
      | rename _time as ssh_time, host as target_host ]
| where ssh_time>=compromise_time AND ssh_time<=compromise_time+3600
| join type=left target_host, principal
    [ search index=linux sourcetype=linux_secure "sudo:" "COMMAND="
      | rename _time as sudo_time, user as principal ]
| table compromise_time, principal, target_host, ssh_time, sudo_time
tuning_guidance: Depends entirely on the underlying IPA-002/IPA-004 tuning; this correlation itself adds confidence rather than noise, so keep the upstream detections reasonably tight.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed identity compromise with endpoint impact: identify every host the principal reached.
Review all sudo/root commands executed across every affected host.
Reset the principal's credentials and force re-authentication fleet-wide.
response_guidance: Full incident response: disable the principal, rotate its keytab/password, review and potentially roll back changes made on every reached host, and hunt for further lateral movement from those hosts.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: IPA Privileged Group Change Propagates to Fleet-Wide Sudo Access
description: Correlates an IPA privileged-group or sudo-rule change (IPA-007 admins group, IPA-012/IPA-013 fleet-wide sudo rules) with subsequent sudo usage by the affected principal across multiple distinct RHEL hosts via SSSD - confirming the privilege expansion was not just configured but actually exercised at fleet scale.

data_sources.name: IPA API/httpd audit + RHEL sudo logs
data_sources.description: Correlates the identity-plane grant with its endpoint-plane exercise across the fleet.

detection_logic: Joins an IPA privilege-grant event to sudo usage by the same principal across multiple distinct hosts within a follow-up window.
spl:
| savedsearch "IPA-007_admins_group_change"
| append [ savedsearch "IPA-012_sudo_rule_all_host" ]
| rename _time as grant_time
| join type=inner target_user
    [ search index=linux sourcetype=linux_secure "sudo:" "COMMAND="
      | rename user as target_user, _time as sudo_time ]
| where sudo_time>=grant_time AND sudo_time<=grant_time+86400
| stats dc(host) as hosts_used values(host) as host_list by target_user, grant_time
| where hosts_used >= 3
tuning_guidance: An approved onboarding of a new fleet administrator will legitimately produce this exact pattern; the value is in flagging it for review, especially when the grant itself (per IPA-007/IPA-012) was not separately confirmed as approved.
investigation_steps: Confirm the underlying IPA grant was approved.
Review the specific sudo commands executed across each host.
Assess whether the scope of hosts touched matches the account's legitimate role.
response_guidance: If the grant was unauthorized, revert it immediately and review all commands executed under the expanded privilege across every touched host.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: AAP Credential Compromise Leads to Fleet-Wide Job Execution
description: Correlates a machine credential being created/modified and newly associated with a job template (AAP-005, AAP-008) with that template subsequently being launched against a broad host scope (AAP-012) within a short window - the full automation-plane attack chain from credential compromise to fleet-wide execution.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream + job events
data_sources.path: Controller API activity stream and job events
data_sources.description: Correlates credential/template configuration changes with subsequent large-scope job launches.

detection_logic: Joins a credential-to-template association event to a subsequent job launch of that template with a large host count.
spl:
| savedsearch "AAP-008_credential_associated_with_template"
| rename _time as association_time
| join type=inner template_name
    [ search index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events job_event="playbook_on_start"
      | rename _time as job_launch_time
      | rex field=_raw "host_count=(?<host_count>\d+)" ]
| where job_launch_time>=association_time AND job_launch_time<=association_time+3600 AND host_count>=25
| table association_time, actor, credential_name, template_name, job_launch_time, host_count
tuning_guidance: Legitimate rapid onboarding of a new automation credential immediately followed by its intended fleet-wide use will also match this pattern; require the upstream AAP-005/AAP-008 events to already be confirmed-approved before treating this correlation as benign.
investigation_steps: Confirm the credential association was approved.
Review exactly what the job did across all targeted hosts.
Assess whether the credential's prior state (before modification) would have had the same fleet-wide reach.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, rotate the credential immediately, review/roll back changes on every targeted host, and audit the actor account.

author: Threat Detection Library

title: AAP Software Supply-Chain Attack (Project SCM to Fleet Change)
description: Correlates the full AAP supply-chain attack chain: a project's SCM URL changes (AAP-017), the project syncs (AAP-018), a job template referencing it launches, and RHEL-side changes matching a known attack pattern (new accounts, SSH keys, or security-control impairment - per the corresponding RHEL detections) are observed on the targeted hosts shortly after.

data_sources.name: AAP activity stream/job events + RHEL auditd
data_sources.description: Ties the platform-side supply-chain change to its confirmed endpoint-side effect.

detection_logic: Chains AAP-017 -> AAP-018 -> a job launch -> a RHEL-side high-confidence indicator (RHEL-014 new UID0, RHEL-017 authorized_keys, RHEL-025/031/035/051 defense impairment) on any host the job touched, all within a bounded time window.
spl:
| savedsearch "AAP-017_project_scm_url_changed"
| rename _time as scm_change_time
| join type=inner project_name
    [ search index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events job_event="playbook_on_start"
      | rename _time as job_launch_time ]
| where job_launch_time>=scm_change_time AND job_launch_time<=scm_change_time+3600
| join type=left host
    [ search index=linux sourcetype=linux_audit (key="ssh_persistence" OR key="identity" OR key="audit_config")
      | rename _time as rhel_indicator_time, host as affected_hosts ]
| table scm_change_time, project_name, job_launch_time, affected_hosts, rhel_indicator_time
tuning_guidance: This chain is deliberately built from already-high-confidence component detections; if all stages fire together the false-positive rate should be very low. Treat any complete chain as an emergency regardless of individual-stage tuning noise.
investigation_steps: Pull the full diff of what changed in the project's playbook content.
Enumerate every host the job template can reach, not just ones already showing a RHEL-side indicator.
Begin full incident response across the affected host population.
response_guidance: Isolate affected hosts, revert the malicious project content, rotate every credential the compromised job template had access to, and rebuild affected hosts from known-good state where warranted.

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Automation Hub Collection Compromise Leads to Fleet Execution
description: Correlates a new collection being uploaded and approved to the certified repository (AAP-026, AAP-027) with a job template/execution environment beginning to reference it and subsequently launching against a broad host scope - the collection-based supply-chain equivalent of RH-X-004.

techniques.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools

data_sources.name: Automation Hub API log + AAP job events
data_sources.path: Hub API log + Controller job events
data_sources.description: Ties collection approval to its downstream consumption and execution.

detection_logic: Joins a collection approval event to a subsequent job launch referencing that collection (via project requirements.yml content or EE image build) with a broad host scope.
spl:
| savedsearch "AAP-027_collection_approved"
| rename _time as approval_time
| join type=inner collection_name
    [ search index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events job_event="playbook_on_start" "collections_used"
      | rename _time as job_launch_time
      | rex field=_raw "host_count=(?<host_count>\d+)" ]
| where job_launch_time>=approval_time AND job_launch_time<=approval_time+604800 AND host_count>=10
| table approval_time, collection_name, job_launch_time, host_count
tuning_guidance: A window of up to a week is used since collections are often approved well before first production use; tighten the window if your environment adopts new collections faster.
investigation_steps: Review the collection's full source code for the modules/roles actually invoked.
Identify who approved it and who uploaded it (self-approval is higher suspicion, per AAP-027).
Assess the scope and actions of every job that used it.
response_guidance: Pull the collection from the certified repository immediately, review/roll back any changes made by jobs that used it, and re-review the approval process.

title: Satellite Repository Compromise Reaches Production RHEL Fleet
description: Correlates the full Satellite supply-chain chain: repository URL/GPG configuration change (SAT-006/SAT-007), synchronization (SAT-008), content view publication and promotion to Production (SAT-010/SAT-012), and package installation on RHEL hosts subscribed to that content view - confirming a compromised upstream source actually reached and was installed on live production systems.

data_sources.name: Satellite/Pulp audit + RHEL package manager logs
data_sources.description: Ties the content-plane compromise to its confirmed installation on endpoints.

detection_logic: Chains SAT-006/SAT-007 -> SAT-008 -> SAT-012 (production promotion) -> package installation events on hosts subscribed to the affected content view, within a bounded time window.
spl:
| savedsearch "SAT-006_repository_url_changed"
| rename _time as config_change_time
| join type=inner repo_name
    [ search index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "content_view_version" "promote" environment="Production"
      | rename _time as promotion_time ]
| where promotion_time>=config_change_time AND promotion_time<=config_change_time+86400
| join type=left
    [ search index=linux sourcetype=dnf_log "Installed"
      | rename _time as install_time, host as affected_hosts ]
| table config_change_time, repo_name, promotion_time, affected_hosts, install_time
tuning_guidance: Built from already-high-confidence component detections (SAT-006/007 have low false-positive rates); a full chain firing should be treated as very high confidence.
investigation_steps: Identify every host that installed packages from the compromised content view since promotion.
Analyze the package content for malicious modification.
Determine the full scope of the compromised upstream source.
response_guidance: Halt further distribution immediately, roll back the content view to the last known-good version, and treat every host that installed the compromised package as requiring investigation/remediation.

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Satellite Remote Execution Attack (Auth to Fleet-Wide Impairment)
description: Correlates a Satellite administrator/API authentication anomaly (SAT-002) with a subsequent large-scope Remote Execution job (SAT-018) containing security-control-impairment or destructive commands (SAT-019/SAT-020) - the complete Satellite-plane attack chain from initial compromise to fleet-wide impact.

data_sources.name: Satellite audit + REX job log
data_sources.description: Ties an authentication compromise indicator to its subsequent destructive use of remote execution.

detection_logic: Joins a SAT-002 compromise indicator to a subsequent SAT-018/019/020 high-risk REX job launch by the same actor within a short window.
spl:
| savedsearch "SAT-002_login_after_failures"
| rename _time as auth_time
| join type=inner actor
    [ search index=satellite sourcetype=foreman:production "job_invocation" "create"
      | rename _time as job_launch_time
      | rex field=_raw "host_count=(?<host_count>\d+)" ]
| where job_launch_time>=auth_time AND job_launch_time<=auth_time+7200 AND host_count>=10
| table auth_time, actor, job_launch_time, host_count
tuning_guidance: This is a deliberately high-confidence chain (a compromised-account indicator directly followed by a fleet-wide destructive-capable action); treat as a top-priority incident whenever it fires.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed account compromise with fleet-wide reach.
Enumerate every host targeted by the job.
Begin incident response across the full affected population immediately.
response_guidance: Cancel the job if still running, disable the compromised account, isolate/investigate every targeted host, and restore any impaired security controls fleet-wide.

author: Threat Detection Library

title: IPA Identity Privilege Expansion Followed by Privileged AAP Automation
description: Correlates an IPA-side identity privilege expansion (IPA-007 admins group, or a new AAP-relevant group membership) with the same identity subsequently authenticating to AAP (if AAP is configured with IPA/LDAP-backed SSO) and launching a privileged job - showing that a single identity-plane compromise can cascade into automation-plane privilege, not just direct RHEL access.

data_sources.name: IPA audit + AAP activity stream
data_sources.description: Correlates an IPA identity-plane privilege change with subsequent AAP-plane authentication and privileged job execution by the same identity.

detection_logic: Joins an IPA-007-style privilege-grant event to a subsequent AAP login (matched on username/email, since AAP and IPA identities are typically federated via SSO) and privileged job launch by that same identity.
spl:
| savedsearch "IPA-007_admins_group_change"
| rename _time as ipa_grant_time, target_user as principal
| join type=inner principal
    [ search index=aap sourcetype=aap:api_access status=200 path="/api/*/login*"
      | rename _time as aap_login_time, user as principal ]
| where aap_login_time>=ipa_grant_time AND aap_login_time<=ipa_grant_time+86400
| join type=left principal
    [ search index=aap sourcetype=aap:job_events job_event="playbook_on_start"
      | rename _time as job_launch_time, launched_by as principal ]
| table ipa_grant_time, principal, aap_login_time, job_launch_time
tuning_guidance: Only meaningful in environments where AAP authentication is federated to IPA/LDAP; if AAP uses fully independent local accounts, use RH-X-002 and AAP-022 as separate, unlinked signals instead.
investigation_steps: Confirm the IPA privilege grant was approved.
Review what AAP-side actions the identity took.
Assess whether IPA-side privilege should have translated to AAP-side privilege at all (a federation/mapping design question worth revisiting).
response_guidance: If the IPA grant was unauthorized, revert it, disable the AAP-side session/token, and audit AAP actions taken under the escalated identity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Coordinated Fleet Modification From Both Satellite and AAP
description: Detects large-scope fleet-modifying actions launched from both Satellite (Remote Execution) and AAP (job execution) within a short window of each other, targeting overlapping host populations. Two independent management planes both taking bulk action against the same fleet segment simultaneously is a pattern far more consistent with a coordinated attack (or an attacker using whichever management plane offered the fastest path) than routine, independently-scheduled operational work.

data_sources.name: Satellite REX log + AAP job events
data_sources.description: Cross-references bulk actions from both management planes by targeted host overlap and timing.

detection_logic: Joins a large-scope Satellite REX job (SAT-018) to a large-scope AAP job (AAP-012) within a short window, computing the overlap between their target host sets.
spl:
| savedsearch "SAT-018_rex_root_broad_scope"
| rename _time as sat_time, job_id as sat_job_id, hosts_targeted as sat_hosts
| eval join_key=1
| join type=inner join_key
    [ search
      | savedsearch "AAP-012_job_all_hosts"
      | rename _time as aap_time, job_id as aap_job_id, host_list as aap_hosts
      | eval join_key=1 ]
| where abs(aap_time-sat_time) <= 1800
| eval overlapping_hosts=mvcount(mvintersect(sat_hosts, aap_hosts))
| where overlapping_hosts >= 3
| table sat_time, sat_job_id, aap_time, aap_job_id, overlapping_hosts
tuning_guidance: Independently-scheduled but coincidentally-overlapping maintenance windows (e.g. both a Satellite patch job and an AAP compliance job scheduled for the same nightly window) are the main false-positive source; correlate against both platforms' documented schedules before escalating.
investigation_steps: Identify the actors behind both jobs and whether they are the same person/team.
Compare the actions taken by each job for a coordinated pattern (e.g. one disables logging while the other installs something).
Assess the full scope of hosts touched by either job.
response_guidance: Treat as a potential coordinated attack pending schedule confirmation: pause both jobs if still running and investigate both management-plane accounts involved.

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Coordinated Defense-Control Impairment Across the Fleet
description: Detects auditd, SELinux, fapolicyd, or firewalld being disabled on multiple distinct RHEL hosts within a short window - regardless of whether the disabling commands were issued host-by-host, via AAP (AAP-014), or via Satellite Remote Execution (SAT-019). This is the fleet-wide capstone correlation: individually, one host losing a security control might be routine troubleshooting; the same loss occurring on several hosts nearly simultaneously is a coordinated defense-evasion campaign almost by definition.

data_sources.name: auditd across the fleet (+ AAP/Satellite job logs where available)
data_sources.description: Aggregates individual-host defense-impairment events (RHEL-025, RHEL-031, RHEL-035, RHEL-042, RHEL-051) fleet-wide and counts distinct hosts affected in a short window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct hosts producing any of the individual defense-impairment indicators (auditd stopped, SELinux permissive/disabled, fapolicyd stopped, firewalld disabled) within a rolling short window, regardless of the initiating management plane.
spl:
index=linux sourcetype=linux_audit (type=SERVICE_STOP unit=auditd) OR (type=MAC_STATUS enforcing=0) OR (type=SERVICE_STOP unit=fapolicyd) OR (type=SERVICE_STOP unit=firewalld)
| eval control_impaired=case(unit="auditd","auditd", unit="fapolicyd","fapolicyd", unit="firewalld","firewalld", type="MAC_STATUS","selinux", 1=1,"unknown")
| bin _time span=15m
| stats dc(host) as hosts_affected values(host) as host_list values(control_impaired) as controls by _time
| where hosts_affected >= 3
tuning_guidance: A genuinely fleet-wide, scheduled hardening-configuration change (e.g. a deliberate, approved rollout that happens to briefly restart these services) is the only plausible legitimate source at this scale; require explicit change-ticket correlation covering the full affected host list.
investigation_steps: Identify every affected host and which control(s) were impaired on each.
Determine the common initiating actor/session/management-plane job across hosts (correlate with AAP-014 and SAT-019).
Check for destructive or persistence activity following the impairment on any affected host.
response_guidance: Treat as a confirmed, active, fleet-wide attack: restore all impaired controls immediately via emergency automation, isolate the most-affected hosts, rotate credentials for whichever management-plane account initiated the change, and begin full incident response.
